mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 55% of instances following a 2%+ MoM drop in IP, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, increasing by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises significantly (Conference Board index up > 5 points) in the month following the unemployment rate trigger, indicating the labor market weakness is temporary.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that will slow economic growth and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real GDP growth accelerates (YoY change in GDPC1 increases by > 1pp) in the quarter following the rate hike trigger, indicating the economy is resilient to higher rates.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year and the unemployment rate is rising, it signals a weakening consumer sector that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and UNRATE rising
failure_condition: Retail sales growth accelerates (YoY change in RSAFS increases by > 2pp) in the month following the trigger, indicating consumer spending remains strong despite the housing and labor market weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth slows by more than 2% year-over-year and the ISM manufacturing PMI falls below 50, signaling a contraction in the manufacturing sector, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 60% of instances following the manufacturing sector contraction trigger, indicating the market is looking through the slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% and the federal funds rate is below 2%, it signals a high-inflation, low-rate environment that will erode the purchasing power of fixed income assets and drive investors into equities, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Real yields on TIPS rise significantly (> 1% increase) in the month following the trigger, indicating fixed income assets are becoming more attractive to investors despite the high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows by more than 1% year-over-year and the unemployment rate is above 6%, it signals a weak labor market that will weigh on consumer spending and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings growth accelerates (> 0.5pp MoM increase) in the month following the trigger, indicating labor market tightness is supporting consumer spending despite the slowing job growth.
